title: Turning from Dodds to Pee Wee Russell in New York
summary: He was always imitative; in New York he shifted to Pee Wee Russell's understated style under Marty Grosz's influence.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Did you get any idea about sitting out and playing your own notes and being more an individualist?

No, I don't think so. I was always a very imitative musician. Later I got away from the New Orleans influence and I came back to Pee Wee Russell. I don't know if you're aware of this, but when I went to New York, this was mainly due to the influence of Mark Groves. And I began to become more interested in Pee Wee Russell, that understated form of playing rather than the extroverted New Orleans style. And then I went for many years imitating Pee Wee instead of imitating Johnny Don. And for a while I was playing very much like Frank Chase plays. I guess not as well, but it was that sort of thing.

It seems to me Marty told me that you had changed your approach. Yes. This was after Marty had been in Chicago, went back to New York and heard you there and came back and said that you enjoyed what you were doing. You seemed to be reasonably happy. There wasn't enough work, maybe that was the problem.
